title: Short bouts of daily movement for people with chronic low back pain
official: Snacktivity and brief movement for everyday life in people with chronic low back pain
summary:
Background and study aims
Chronic low back pain is common and can make it difficult for people to stay active. Although physical activity is recommended, many people find structured exercise programmes difficult to follow due to pain, fatigue, or lack of confidence.
This study aims to test whether a different approach encouraging very short, flexible bouts of movement throughout the day (“Snacktivity”) is practical, acceptable, and potentially helpful for people with chronic low back pain.

Who can participate?
Adults aged 18 years or older with chronic low back pain lasting longer than 3 months can take part. Participants must be living independently and able to engage in light movement. People with serious spinal conditions, specific causes of back pain, or major health issues that limit movement will not be eligible.

What does the study involve?
Participants will be randomly allocated to one of two groups:
1. A Snacktivity group, involving a 6-week programme encouraging short, frequent movement in daily life, supported by an introductory session and weekly check-ins
2. A comparison group, receiving standard advice for managing low back pain
Participants will complete questionnaires at the start of the study, after 6 weeks, and at a 12-week follow-up. Some participants may also take part in interviews about their experiences.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants may benefit from increased confidence, improved understanding of movement, and a better ability to manage daily activity with back pain.
Risks are expected to be low but may include temporary increases in pain, discomfort, or fatigue when moving. Participants are encouraged to adapt or stop activities if needed.

Where is the study run from?
The study is run from the University of Birmingham (UK), with participation taking place in the community and/or online.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
September 2026 to October 2027

Who is funding the study?
University of Birmingham (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Dr Andrew Soundy, A.A.Soundy@bham.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults aged ≥18 years
2. Diagnosis of CLBP (≥3 months duration). CLBP will be defined as pain in the lumbar region persisting for 3 months or longer 
3. Back pain which is not attributable to a specific cause, i.e., people with non-specific CLBP will be recruited
4. Living independently in the community
5. Able to stand and move with or without discomfort and able to engage with light physical movement as part of daily activities
6. Able to provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Acute low back pain (<3 months)
2. Serious spinal pathology (e.g., fracture, malignancy, infection) or uncontrolled comorbidities (including major psychiatric conditions, uncontrolled diabetes or heart failure)
3. Specific causes of CLBP, e.g., lumbar radiculopathy
4. Neurological conditions severely limiting movement
5. Current participation in structured exercise rehabilitation (>2 sessions/week)
6. Pregnancy
